walkthroughs.body_html:
Religious & Ethical Teachings about Peace & Conflict — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religious & Ethical Teachings about Peace & Conflict brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religious & Ethical Teachings about Peace & Conflict.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.

mcqs.q: What does karma mean in Hindu and Buddhist thought?
options: Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
Karma is when bad things happen to bad people as punishment.
The principle that actions have moral consequences shaping future experience or rebirth — not fate, but ethical cause and effect built into reality.

mcqs.q: What does Buddhism teach about suffering?
options: Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
Karma is a god who decides what happens to you.
All existence involves dukkha (suffering/unsatisfactoriness), caused by tanha (craving and attachment); ending craving leads to liberation from suffering.
Buddhism teaches that life is nothing but pain and misery.
